Context & Sources

Access did not arrive everywhere at once.

A historical regional dataset retained from the fieldbook. Missing years are explicitly marked.

This map uses official World Bank regional aggregates for internet use to show how digital adoption spread unevenly across the world. The slider spans 2000 to 2025, and the comparable regional series begins in 2005, so the first few years show the pre-series lead-in before large-scale adoption accelerates.

Selected year 2025. Regional values follow in the table.

Markers show regional internet-use percentages. Larger markers indicate greater adoption; exact stored values are listed below.

Global context

The stakes extend beyond one portfolio.

International Telecommunication Union · November 10, 2024

79% of people aged 15 to 24 worldwide use the Internet

The ITU reported on November 10, 2024 that youth internet use is 13 percentage points higher than for the rest of the population, but the gap by income level is still large.

Read the source

WHO Regional Office for Europe · September 25, 2024

11% of adolescents showed signs of problematic social media use in 2022

WHO reported on September 25, 2024 that this figure rose from 7% in 2018 to 11% in 2022, and another 12% of adolescents were at risk of problematic gaming.

Read the source

WHO Regional Office for Europe · March 27, 2024

1 in 6 school-aged children experienced cyberbullying

WHO reported on March 27, 2024 that cyberbullying increased between 2018 and 2022, with reports of being cyberbullied rising to 15% for boys and 16% for girls.

Read the source

UNICEF Innocenti · June 2025

1 in 5 10-year-olds in 51 countries lacked internet access at home in 2021

UNICEF Innocenti reported in its June 2025 digital world report that the share increased to two in five in the low- and middle-income countries included in the study.

Read the source
